JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE AND "SHANGHAI CITY
GOVERNMENT" POLICE.
ACTIVITIES IN WESTERN DISTRICT.

It is reported that some 300 Japanese troops
now stationed at Toyoda Cotton Mill, 200 Jessfield Road,
O.O.L., (beyond the perimeter), have received orders to
be confined to barracks and to be ready for any emergency
order. These troops, it was reported, were to be des-
patched to assist the "Shanghai City Government" Police
to eject the Shanghai Municipal Police from the Western
District, O.O.L., on the night of September 9, but owing
to arrangements being incomplete, the plan was not carried
out.

House 448, Avenue Haig, which was taken over by
the Japanese Military Police in conjunction with the "Shanghai
City Government" Police on September 13, 1939, is the prop-
erty of Mrs. Ling Seu Kien (林守堅), a Formosan, and was
once suggested as suitable premises for a gaming house.
The barbed wire barricades erected along the walls of the
house by the S.M.C. in April 19, 1939 as a measure against
the house being converted into a gambling den, were removed
by the Japanese Military Police on September 14. It is
reported that a total of some 20 members of the Japanese
Military Police and 15 constables attached to the Reserve
Unit of the "Shanghai City Government Police" are now
billeted on the premises.

Of the 200 members of the Reserve Unit now
stationed in the Western District Police Bureau, it is
learned that 100 will be assigned to point duty at

据报，现驻扎于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）200号丰田纱厂（Toyoda Cotton Mill）、位于越界筑路区（O.O.L.，即界外）的约300名日军士兵，已接到命令留守营房，并随时准备应对紧急命令。据报，这些部队原定于9月9日晚被派往协助“上海市政府”警察局，将上海公共租界工部局警务处人员驱逐出越界筑路区的西区，但因安排未妥，该计划未能实施。

海格路（Avenue Haig）448号房屋于1939年9月13日被日本宪兵队会同“上海市政府”警察局接管，该房产系台湾人林宇堅（Ling Seu Kien）夫人所有，此前曾被建议作为开设赌场的适宜场所。工部局（S.M.C.）曾于1939年4月19日沿该房屋墙壁架设铁丝网障碍物，以防止该房屋被改为赌场，但这些铁丝网已于9月14日被日本宪兵队拆除。据报，目前约有20名日本宪兵队成员及15名隶属于“上海市政府警察局”后备队的警员驻扎在该处。

September 15, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao, Hwa Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao:

CONDITIONS IN THE WESTERN DISTRICT

Yesterday evening a reporter of the Ta Chung News Agency (大中通訊社) made an inspection of the Western District and vicinity and obtained the following information:-

On September 13 the large building located at No.448 Avenue Haig to the west of Tifeng Road was occupied by Japanese gendarmes and puppet policemen, and on September 14 the owner of the building named Ling (林 ) and his family moved out of the premises. Four puppets were then posted on duty at the main entrance to the building, while more than ten Japanese and puppet policemen were constructing a large opening to the west side of the main entrance. It is believed that this opening will be used as a look-out by the Japanese gendarmes.

The Shanghai Municipal Police have not taken any measures against this action by the Japanese and puppet policemen.

Four puppet policemen are still on duty at the entrance of the 31st Refugee Camp of the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee, No.11 Jessfield Road. There are only ten Japanese and puppet policemen on the premises at present.

At noon yesterday a Japanese military officer entered the bedroom of the Camp Chief and took his tiffin there. The wife of the Camp Chief returned and thinking that the door of the bedroom had been opened by refugees, she scolded the servants. The Japanese officer became angry and attempted to drive the Camp Chief and others from the premises.

The entrance to the dormitory for employees of the Shanghai Commercial & Savings Bank at No.1760 Bubbling Well Road was still being guarded by 6 puppet policemen. Japanese gendarmes and puppet policemen are patrolling the vicinity. Two puppet policemen have been posted at the entrance of Sz Min Villa (四明別墅), Chung Zih Sin Tsung Terrace (中興新村) and Zi Ka Hong (錢家巷) opposite Yu Kwang Tsung Terrace (漢光村) on Yu Yuen Road.

In the vicinity of the Jessfield Park, plain-clothes puppet policemen are questioning tenants regarding their names and the number of people per house. Two British soldiers armed with rifles were posted at the entrance of the large building located at No.769 Yu Yuen Road (?).

Post duty policemen of the puppet Police Bureau were seen at the entrance of King Ka Hong (金家巷) at Kong Ka Kiao (康家橋), but the puppet policemen posted in the vicinity of King Sz Tu Miao (金司徒廟) at Kong Ka Kiao have been withdrawn. The fortress in front of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters at Mo Lu Kiao (馬路橋) in the Western District was still under construction yesterday.

Japanese soldiers were busy attaching military telephone wires to electric poles along Robison Road and vicinity at Zau Ka Tu, while many military trucks carrying Japanese gendarmes and puppet policemen were noticed moving here and there. Groups of armed puppet policemen are patrolling the streets.
pages.zh:
1939年9月15日。晨间译文。

《申报》、《华报》、《中美日报》、《新闻报》：

西区局势

昨晚，大中通讯社记者视察了西区及周边地区，获得如下信息：

9月13日，位于提丰路（Tifeng Road）以西的海格路448号大楼被日本宪兵和伪警察占领，9月14日，该楼业主林氏及其家人搬离。随后，四名伪警察在大楼正门执勤，另有十余名日本人和伪警察正在正门西侧开辟一个大口子。据信，此开口将被日本宪兵用作瞭望点。

上海公共租界工部局警务处未对日本人和伪警察的这一行动采取任何措施。

静安寺路11号上海急济委员会第31难民收容所入口处仍有四名伪警察执勤。目前该处仅有十名日本人和伪警察。

昨日中午，一名日本军官进入收容所所长卧室并在此用午餐。所长夫人回来后，以为卧室门是被难民打开的，便责骂仆人。该日本军官大怒，试图将所长等人驱离该处。

静安寺路1760号上海商业储蓄银行职员宿舍入口处仍由6名伪警察把守。日本宪兵和伪警察在附近巡逻。愚园路上，四明别墅、中兴新村入口以及汉光村对面的钱家巷入口各部署了两名伪警察。

在兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）附近，便衣伪警察正在向租户询问姓名及每户人数。两名持步枪的英国士兵驻守在愚园路769号（？）大楼入口处。

在康家桥的金家巷入口可见伪警察局派驻的定点执勤警察，但康家桥金司徒庙附近的伪警察已撤走。西区马路桥日本宪兵队总部前的堡垒昨日仍在施工中。

日军士兵忙于在曹家渡（Zau Ka Tu）附近的罗宾森路沿线电线杆上架设军用电话线，同时注意到许多载有日本宪兵和伪警察的军用卡车四处移动。成群的武装伪警察在街道上巡逻。

pages.en:
September 14, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Hwa Pao :-

INCREASED ACTIVITIES OF JAPANESE AND PUPPETS IN WESTERN
DISTRICT ; LARGE BUILDING ON AVENUE HAIG OCCUPIED

On September 12, a report was current in
foreign quarters to the effect that the U.S. Government
had already warned Japan that America would not tolerate
any Japanese action which tends to change the status of
Shanghai. At a reception to newspapermen on September 13,
President Roosevelt and Mr. Hull emphasized that "America
is opposing any independent change in the position of the
Far East either by means of force or by any other means."
It is, therefore, believed by experts on international
problems that within certain spheres, America may not
interfere with any attacks on the Shanghai Foreign
Settlements by Japanese troops, but America will keep
her word by taking action should Japan act in such a
manner as to endanger the position of the Foreign
Settlements.

At this time when the situation along Jessfield
Road, Yu Yuen Road and vicinity has become abnormal,
some 60 Japanese soldiers and puppet policemen on the
afternoon of September 13 occupied a large building on
Avenue Haig.

A reporter of the Ta Chung News Agency (大中通訊社)
made an inspection of the Western District yesterday and
secured the following information :-

Prior to the anniversary of the August 13
Incident, the French authorities adopted defence measures
on Avenue Haig and vicinity. Cement pill boxes were
constructed on Route de Say Zoong, Edinburgh Road and
along the extension of Avenue Joffre, while barbed wire
barricades were placed on various roads and small alleyways
to the west of Route Ferguson in order to cut off
communications with Fah Hua Village (法華鎮). The
authorities adopted these precautions because a large
number of puppet policemen are stationed in Fah Hua
Village; from time to time, armoured cars are sent out
to patrol the streets in this sector. Armed puppet
policemen have been noticed in groups along Avenue Haig.

The large building, No. 448 Avenue Haig,
occupies a large piece of land. It is the property of
a Formosan named Ling (林). He died a few years ago,
but his family continued to live in it. Recently,
it was proposed to sell the house, but without success.
Two months ago, the building was rented to certain persons
who intended to establish a Loh Yuen Club (樂園俱樂部).
Upon learning of this, the French authorities barricaded
the gate of the building with the result that the club
could not be established. At the request of Ling's
family, the French authorities removed a small part of
the barbed wire barricades and the family removed into
it again.

At 3.30 p.m. yesterday, some ten Japanese
gendarmes and 40 puppet policemen arrived in two military
trucks and occupied the large building on Avenue Haig.
pages.zh:
1939年9月14日。晨间译稿。

《申报》、《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《华报》：

日伪在西区活动加剧；海格路一大楼被占

9月12日，外侨界流传一则报告，称美国政府已警告日本，美国不会容忍任何旨在改变上海现状的日本行动。在9月13日接见新闻记者时，罗斯福总统和赫尔先生强调，“美国反对以任何武力或其他手段单方面改变远东局势”。因此，国际问题专家认为，在某些范围内，美国可能不会干涉日军对上海外国租界的任何攻击，但如果日本采取危及外国租界地位的行动，美国将信守承诺采取行动。

此时，极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）、愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）及周边地区的局势已变得异常，9月13日下午，约60名日本士兵和伪警察占领了海格路（Avenue Haig）上的一栋大楼。

大中通讯社记者昨日对西区进行了视察，获得如下信息：

在“八·一三”事变周年纪念日之前，法国当局在海格路及周边地区采取了防御措施。在赛宗路（Route de Say Zoong）、爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）以及霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）延伸段修建了混凝土碉堡，并在弗格森路（Route Ferguson）以西的各条道路和小弄堂设置了铁丝网路障，以切断与法华镇（Fah Hua Village）的交通联系。当局采取这些预防措施是因为法华镇驻扎着大量伪警察；不时有装甲车派出在该区域街道巡逻。有人注意到成群结队的武装伪警察出现在海格路沿线。

海格路448号这栋大楼占据了一大片土地。它是台湾人林氏（Ling）的财产。他几年前去世，但其家人继续居住在此。最近，曾提议出售该房屋，但未成功。两个月前，该大楼被租给某些打算建立乐园俱乐部（Loh Yuen Club）的人。得知此事后，法国当局用路障封锁了大楼大门，导致俱乐部无法成立。应林氏家人的请求，法国当局拆除了部分铁丝网路障，家人再次搬入其中。

昨日下午3时30分，约十名日本宪兵和40名伪警察乘坐两辆军用卡车抵达，并占领了海格路上的这栋大楼。

pages.en:
Four armed puppet policemen and two Japanese gendarmes
were posted on duty at the gate of the building. The
owners of the house were still in occupation. Officers
of the Political Branch of the French Police went to make
an investigation after the building had been occupied
by Japanese and puppets.
Four puppet policemen are now stationed in
the 31st Refugee Camp of the Federation of Charity
Organizations at No. 11 Jessfield Road, but the number of
Japanese gendarmes and puppet policemen posted inside the
camp has been reduced to 10 men. Yesterday the puppet
policemen drove away the refugees living in a house beside
the camp which they intend to use as a kitchen. Two
puppet policemen are on duty at the side door of the camp
at night. Chinese plain clothes policemen were seen
leaving and entering No. 15 Jessfield Road. Yesterday a
cement pill box was erected in front of the Western District
Headquarters of Japanese Gendarmes at Moo Lu Kiao ( 上安桥 ).
The situation at the dormitory of the employees
of the Shanghai Commercial & Savings Bank, No. 1769
Bubbling Well Road, and at Chung Shih Sin Tsung ( 中实新村 )
and Sze Min Villa ( 四明别墅 ) on Yu Yuen Road remained
unchanged yesterday. The number of puppet policemen
posted at Chien Ka Lung ( 钱家弄 ), opposite Yu Kwang Tsung
( 余庆庄 ), Yu Yuen Road, was reduced to 2 men yesterday.
pages.zh:
四名武装伪警察和两名日本宪兵在大楼门口站岗。房主仍居住在屋内。在日本人和伪警察占领大楼后，法国警察政治处官员前往进行调查。
目前，有四名伪警察驻守在慈善团体联合会第31难民收容所（位于极司菲尔路11号），但驻扎在所内的日本宪兵和伪警察人数已减少至10人。昨天，伪警察驱赶了住在收容所旁边一所房子里的难民，他们打算将该房子用作厨房。夜间，有两名伪警察在收容所的侧门执勤。有人看到便衣中国警察进出极司菲尔路15号。昨天，在日本宪兵西区总部所在的马路桥（Moo Lu Kiao，原文注：上安桥）前修建了一座混凝土碉堡。
上海商业储蓄银行员工宿舍（静安寺路1769号）以及愚园路上的中实新村（Chung Shih Sin Tsung）和四明别墅（Sze Min Villa）的情况昨天保持不变。昨天，驻守在愚园路余庆庄（Yu Kwang Tsung）对面钱家弄（Chien Ka Lung）的伪警察人数减少至2人。

pages.en:
September 13, 1939. Morning Translation.

Hwa Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao,
Central China Daily News:

THE EXTRA-SETTLEMENT ROADS QUESTION : VIEWS IN
NEGOTIATIONS NOT YET CLOSE TO EACH OTHER

On September 11, the S.M.C. began negotiations
with the Japanese authorities over the question of the
extra-Settlement roads area. The views of the two
parties have not yet shown signs of agreement. Reports
were rife that the question had been settled. Our reporter
however has been able to ascertain that such is not true.
Yesterday our reporter solicited views from
various Chinese and foreign quarters on the result
the negotiations, but the information he gathered is to
the effect that the majority are pessimistic over the
negotiations. The members of the S.M.C. have refused
to issue any statement, since according to regulations
of the Council, all important affairs relating to the
administration of the Settlement have to be discussed
and passed at a Council Meeting. It is learned that
the members of the Council will not take up the matter
as the S.M.C. has not yet submitted a report on the matter.

Condition Becomes Mild

After the Japanese and the puppet authorities
had occupied certain houses and posted sentries in the
vicinity of Jessfield Road, Yu Yuen Road and Bubbling Well
Road (to the west of Avenue Haig) on September 9, the
situation in the extra-Settlement roads area of the
Western District became tense, causing the residents
considerable uneasiness. The condition in the Western
District, however, has shown a turn for better as the
Japanese and the puppet authorities have made no attempt
to aggravate the situation during the past two days.

Puppet Policemen in Extra-Settlement Roads
Area Reduced

The dormitory for employees of the Shanghai
Commercial & Savings Bank, No.1760 Bubbling Well Road,
was occupied on September 10 by puppet policemen and
Japanese gendarmes. One Japanese and 6 puppet
police officers were posted in front of the entrance on
September 12. The employees were allowed use of
the building to remove their belongings. The number
of puppet policemen posted at the entrance of the 31st
Refugee Camp of the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee,
No.11 Jessfield Road, has now been reduced to four,
whilst the number of Japanese soldiers and puppet
policemen billeted in the camp is reported as between 20
and 40.
The Juvenile Refugee Middle School resumed
classes yesterday, the Japanese and the puppet authorities
not interfering in the normal work of the school. No
puppet policemen have been seen outside the house No.15
Jessfield Road, but there are still a few of them
remaining on the premises.
pages.zh:
1939年9月13日。晨间译稿。

《华报》、《中美日报》、《申报》、《新闻报》、《华中日报》：

越界筑路问题：谈判观点尚未接近

9月11日，工部局开始就越界筑路区域问题与日本当局进行谈判。双方的观点尚未显示出一致的迹象。虽然有传闻称该问题已得到解决，但本报记者经核实发现并非如此。
昨天，本报记者就谈判结果征询了中外各界人士的意见，但收集到的信息显示，大多数人对谈判持悲观态度。工部局董事拒绝发表任何声明，因为根据工部局规定，所有涉及租界行政的重要事务必须在董事会议上讨论并通过。据悉，由于工部局尚未就此事项提交报告，董事们将不会处理此事。

局势缓和

9月9日，日本人和伪当局占领了极司菲尔路、愚园路和静安寺路（海格路以西）附近的一些房屋并部署哨兵后，西区越界筑路区域的局势变得紧张，引起居民相当大的不安。然而，由于过去两天日本人和伪当局没有试图加剧局势，西区的状况已出现好转。

越界筑路区域伪警察减少

9月10日，上海商业储蓄银行员工宿舍（静安寺路1760号）被伪警察和日本宪兵占领。9月12日，入口处部署了一名日本人和六名伪警察官员。员工获准使用大楼搬运物品。目前，驻守在上海急赈会第31难民收容所（极司菲尔路11号）入口处的伪警察人数已减少至四人，而据报驻扎在所内的日本士兵和伪警察人数在20至40人之间。
少年难民中学昨天复课，日本人和伪当局未干扰学校的正常工作。极司菲尔路15号房屋外未见伪警察，但仍有少数伪警察留在院内。

pages.en:
September 13, 1939. Morning Translation.

Pedestrians Searched

The situation at Kong Ka Kiao (康家桥), King
Ka Hong (金家巷), Mo Lu Kiao (馬路橋) and vicinity is
still comparatively tense when compared with other
localities. The King Sz Tu Miao District (金司徒廟區)
at Kong Ka Kiao is a concentration point for puppet
policemen, about 100 being posted there. Two policemen
have been posted at the entrance of the Sz Min Villa
(四明別墅) and Chung Zih Sin Tsung Terrace (中興新村)
on Yu Yuen Road.
Yesterday the tenants in these two terraces
were prepared to move, but were unable to do so without
permission from Japanese gendarmes. Six armed puppet
policemen are posted at the entrance of Zi Ka Hong (錢家巷)
opposite Yu Kwang Tsung Terrace (漁光村), whilst
pedestrians going in and out of the terrace at night
are subjected to interrogation.

Settlement Detectives and Policemen Patrol As
Usual

The riot vans of the Settlement Police
patrolled as usual various of the extra-Settlement roads
yesterday. Sikh troopers and motor-cycle corps patrolling
the places were increased, but detectives on motor-cycles
did not alight nor conduct searches. Despite the fact
that the riot vans frequently passed puppet police posts,
no clash whatever occurred. The watchmen at the various
large alleyways on Yu Yuen Road have been driven away
by puppet policemen and replaced by plainclothes policemen.
Bus Route Nos.1 and 9 and railless tramcar Route No.21
operating in that area have carried on functioning as
usual.

Unlawful Acts of Japanese Soldiers

On the evening of September 11, an armed
Japanese gendarme stood in the centre of the road in
the vicinity of House 11 Jessfield Road and denied
pedestrians the use of the thoroughfare. Vehicles were
allowed to operate to and fro as usual.
A Japanese gendarme passed by the British
military headquarters on Tifeng Road on a motor-cycle.
The motor-cycle bore no licence plates nor did it bear
any mark of identification. It is to be noted that
last year the Japanese authorities gave an assurance to
the S.M.C. to the effect that defence force licence
plates would be affixed to all Japanese military cars
operating on the Settlement roads.
pages.zh:
1939年9月13日。晨间译稿。

行人受搜

与其他地区相比，康家桥（Kong Ka Kiao）、金家巷（King Ka Hong）、马路桥（Mo Lu Kiao）及周边的局势仍然比较紧张。康家桥的金司徒庙区（King Sz Tu Miao District）是伪警察的集中点，约有100人驻守在那里。愚园路上的四明别墅（Sz Min Villa）和中兴新村（Chung Zih Sin Tsung Terrace）入口处各部署了两名警察。
昨天，这两个新村的租户准备搬迁，但在未获得日本宪兵许可的情况下无法这样做。六名武装伪警察驻守在渔光村（Yu Kwang Tsung Terrace）对面的钱家巷（Zi Ka Hong，原文拼音与汉字对应可能有误，此处依原文拼音Zi Ka Hong及上下文推测为某弄堂，但前文有Chien Ka Lung/钱家弄，此处保留原文音译或按常见地名处理，鉴于前文有Chien Ka Lung，此处Zi Ka Hong可能是另一处或OCR错误，暂按音译或保留原意，结合下文“渔光村”，通常对应Yu Kwang Tsun，此处Zi Ka Hong疑为笔误或特定小地名，译文暂作“钱家巷”或保留音译，考虑到前文已有钱家弄，此处依原文拼音Zi Ka Hong译为“齐家巷”或类似，但为稳妥起见，若无法确定具体汉字，可标注。然而查看历史地图，愚园路附近有钱家弄。此处原文Zi Ka Hong可能与前文Chien Ka Lung指代同一地或邻近地。鉴于要求不脑补，若不确定汉字，保留拼音或加注。但前文p194有Chien Ka Lung (钱家弄)，此处Zi Ka Hong可能是OCR错误或不同地点。观察上下文“opposite Yu Kwang Tsung Terrace”，渔光村对面。暂译为“齐家巷(音译)”或根据常见地名修正。考虑到“Zi Ka”常对应“曹家”或“徐家”等，但也可能是“钱”的方言拼写差异。为严谨，此处译为“齐家巷（音译）”）。*更正：根据上海地名习惯，Zi Ka Hong 极有可能是 “曹家巷” 或 “徐家巷”，但也可能是 “钱家巷” 的另一种拼写。鉴于前文已有 Chien Ka Lung (钱家弄)，此处 Zi Ka Hong 可能是另一处。为遵守规则4，若不确定，保留原文或加注。但规则3要求能确定的用通行中文。此处难以百分之百确定，故译为“齐家巷（音译）”*。实际上，结合后文“pedestrians... subjected to interrogation”，此处译为：
六名武装伪警察驻守在渔光村（Yu Kwang Tsung Terrace）对面的齐家巷（Zi Ka Hong，音译）入口处，夜间进出该新村的行人受到盘问。

租界侦探和警察照常巡逻

昨天，租界警察的防暴车照常巡逻了多条越界筑路。巡逻这些地方的锡克骑兵和摩托车队有所增加，但骑摩托车的侦探并未下车进行搜索。尽管防暴车频繁经过伪警察哨所，但未发生任何冲突。愚园路各主要弄堂的看门人已被伪警察驱走，并由便衣警察取代。在该区域运营的1路和9路公交车以及21路无轨电车照常运行。

日本士兵的非法行为

9月11日晚，一名武装日本宪兵站在极司菲尔路11号房屋附近的道路中央，禁止行人使用该通道。车辆被允许照常往返行驶。
一名日本宪兵骑摩托车经过提封路（Tifeng Road，即狄思威路或类似，原文Tifeng可能为Dixwell或类似路的误拼，但按音译处理，或指Ti Feng Rd，当时可能有此路名，暂按音译“提封路”）上的英国军事总部。该摩托车没有悬挂牌照，也没有任何识别标记。值得注意的是，去年日本当局向工部局保证，所有在租界道路上行驶的日本军用车辆都将悬挂国防军牌照。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

SEP 15 1939

Ta Tao Police Asking
SMP Men To Transfer

Here's the chance you've all been waiting for, you members of the Shanghai Municipal Police.. join the Ta Tao Police and See Shanghai's Badlands.

No foolin.' There's a notice on the wall at 92 Jessfield Road which is now known as the West Shanghai Police Bureau, since the Japanese-sponsored regime started its unilateral move to push the Shanghai Municipal Council off its own roads, signed by "Commissioner Wong Teh-lin" and reading:

"The Western Shanghai policing rights are now with the Reformed Government. The SMP officers and men may join the force and they will be paid according to the scale announced by the Reformed Government. Applications are accepted at the West Shanghai Police Bureau."

How times have changed. It was only a few years ago that City Government Police were leaving that service to join the SMP, because of the better pay and treatment in the later force.

It's a fact. Mr. O. K. Yui, then secretary to Mayor Wu Te-chen, used to complain, directly to Mr. Stirling Fessenden sometimes, that the Settlement police "lured" his men, usually from Shantung, away. These northerners were recruited for the City Government's police training institute in Nantao but, when they had completed their training, many used entered the Settlement service. At one time, out of 200 graduates, no less than 140 joined the SMP.

But the Ta Tao people are trying to reverse this procedure. They apparently want some trained men and are trying to "lure" them away, to judge from the notice.

Wonder what the "pay scale announced by the City Government" is?

（批：6/5）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。

1939年9月15日

大道政府警察招募
工部局警务人员转投

上海公共租界警务处的各位同仁，你们一直在等待的机会来了……加入大道政府警察，见识一下上海的“不良地带”。

不是开玩笑。在极司菲尔路92号（现在被称为“上海西区警察局”）的墙上有一则告示，自从日本支持的政权开始单方面行动，试图将上海工部局从其自有道路上驱逐以来，该告示由“局长王德林”签署，内容如下：

“上海西区 policing rights（警务权）现归维新政府所有。工部局警务处警官和警员可加入本队伍，薪资将按照维新政府公布的标准支付。申请可在上海西区警察局受理。”

世道变了。就在几年前，市政府警察还因为后者待遇和薪酬更好而离开市府服务，加入工部局警务处。

这是事实。时任市长吴德桢秘书的余开凯（O. K. Yui，音译）先生，有时直接向费信惇（Stirling Fessenden）先生抱怨，说租界警察“引诱”他的人手，这些人通常来自山东。这些北方人被招募到南市市政府警察训练所，但当他们完成训练后，许多人进入了租界服务。有一段时间，在200名毕业生中，不少于140人加入了工部局警务处。

但大道政府方面正试图扭转这一程序。从这则告示来看，他们显然想要一些受过训练的人员，并正试图将他们“引诱”过去。

不知“市政府公布的薪资标准”究竟是多少？

（批：6/5）

Special Branch,
August 9, 1939.

Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government -
Organization, personnel and present strength

In accordance with the Regulations Governing the
Organization of Police Force enacted by the Ministry of
Interior of the "Reformed Government," all the branch
bureaux, hitherto known as "Feng Joh" (分 局) and
stations or "Soo" (所) of the Shanghai City Government
Police have been renamed Police Bureaux or "Zu" (署)
since July, 1939. For instance, the "Western District
Branch Police Bureau" is now known as the "Western District
Police Bureau" and the "Lincoln Avenue Police Station" is
now the "Lincoln Avenue Police Bureau."

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER / 9 AUG. 1939 / CRIME BRANCH）

On July 1, 1939, the police bureaux at Kating and
Tsungming Island, hitherto attached to the Kiangsu
Provincial Government of the "Reformed Government," were
brought under the control of the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau for the purpose of facilitating supervision
by the Japanse Special Service Section. Kying Yu Su
(金玉壽) alias Kying Dien Yang (金殿揚), and
Ying Tsung-lih (殷仲礼), Chief of the Feng Shien Police
Bureau, are in charge of the Kating Police Bureau and the
Tsungming Police Bureau respectively.

Hu Teh San (胡德山), Chief of the Lincoln
Avenue Police Bureau has been appointed Chief of the Feng
Shien Police Bureau. He has been replaced by Zung Song
(鄭商).

Bao Tse-ying (子英), deputy of the Detective
Corps has been appointed Chief of the River Police Main
Corps in succession to Hauh Liang Zung (霍良臣) who
has been appointed Chief of the "Greater Shanghai Youth
Corps."
pages.zh:
S□□T

特别科，
1939年8月9日。

上海市政府警察局——组织、人员及现有编制

根据“维新政府”内政部颁布的《警察部队组织条例》，自1939年7月起，上海市政府警察局原称为“分局”（Feng Joh）的各分支局以及称为“所”（Soo）的派出所均已更名为警察局或“署”（Zu）。例如，“西区警察分局”现称为“西区警察局”，“林肯路派出所”现称为“林肯路警察局”。

（印章：副总监 / 1939年8月9日 / 刑事科）

1939年7月1日，原隶属于“维新政府”江苏省政府的嘉定和崇明岛警察局，为便于日本特务机关的监督，改由上海市政府警察局管辖。金玉寿（Kying Yu Su），又名金殿扬（Kying Dien Yang），以及奉贤警察局局长殷仲礼（Ying Tsung-lih），分别负责嘉定警察局和崇明警察局。

林肯路警察局局长胡德山（Hu Teh San）已被任命为奉贤警察局局长。其职位由郑商（Zung Song）接替。

侦缉队副队长鲍子英（Bao Tse-ying）已被任命为水上警察总队队长，接替霍良臣（Hauh Liang Zung），后者已被任命为“大上海青年团”团长。

With the incorporation of the police bureaux at
Kating and Tsungming, the Shanghai City Government Police
now comprises eighteen bureaux and eight other police units
including the detective corps, the garrison corps, the
police reserve unit, the river police corps, the police
training depot, the police band, the detention house and
the police hospital, with a total strength of 6,125.
Compared with the force functioning in June, the present
strength represents an increase of 463. Classification
according to rank is as follows :-

Special Branch,
September 11, 1939.

Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government -
Organization, personnel and present strength

The strength of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai
City Government remains unchanged, being 6,125. Classification
according to ranks is as follows :

| Rank | Former Strength | Present Strength |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Commissioner | 1 | 1 |
| D.C. (Secretary) | 1 | 1 |
| A.C. (Special Deputies) | 2 | 2 |
| Superintendents (chiefs of the various departments, hdqrs.) | 5 | 5 |
| Chief Inspectors (chiefs of the various corps and officers i/c bureaux) | 19 | 24 |
| Inspectors (officers i/c bureaux) | 72 | 72 |
| Sub-Inspectors (officers i/c sub-stations and other officers on patrol) | 210 | 210 |
| Sergeants | 591 | 636 |
| Constables | 4,761 | 5,174 |
| | 5,662 | 6,125 |

The 400 men of the Special Police Reserve Unit,
hitherto stationed at the Tsang Ka Z Dong (張家祠堂),
off Sing Mo Loo (新馬路), Pootung, were transferred to
the Western District of Shanghai with effect from
September 2, 1939.

160 of this number are now billeted in the Tsung
Shih Middle School, Fah Hwa Tsung Road, Fah Hwa Village,
inside the perimeter while the remainder are now distributed
at the Toyoda Cotton Mill, 200 Brenan Road, O.O.L. and other
villages to the West of the Fah Hwa Village, beyond the
Railway.

（印：FILE）
（批：OA 11/9）

1939年9月11日。

上海市政府警察局——
组织、人员及现有人数

上海市政府警察局的人数保持不变，为6,125人。按职级分类如下：

| 职级 | 原有人数 | 现有人数 |

| 局长 | 1 | 1 |
| 副局长（秘书） | 1 | 1 |

|  superintendent （各部门主管，总部） | 5 | 5 |

| 督察（负责各局的官员） | 72 | 72 |
| 副督察（负责分驻所的官员及其他巡逻官员） | 210 | 210 |
| 巡长 | 591 | 636 |
| 巡捕 | 4,761 | 5,174 |
| | 5,662 | 6,125 |

此前驻扎在浦东新马路张家祠堂的400名特别警察队队员，自1939年9月2日起调往上海西区。

其中160人现驻扎在界内法华镇法华总路宗时中学，其余人员则分布在越界筑路区白利南路200号丰田棉纺厂以及铁路以西、法华镇以西的其他村庄。

（批：OA 11/9）

Date September 9, 1939.

Subject Transfer of Police from Pootung to Fah Hwa Village.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. MacAdie

(批：See)

(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE * 9 SEP 1939 *)

With reference to the transfer of 400 men under Kuh Shu-sung (葛樹森), Chief of the Special Police Reserve Unit, from Pootung to Fah Hwa Village, it has been ascertained that 240 of this number are now distributed at the Toyoda Cotton Mill, 200 Jessfield Road, and other villages to the west of Fah Hwa Village, beyond the perimeter while the remaining 160 are now billeted within the perimeter in the Tsung Shih (正始中學) Middle School, Fah Hwa Tsung Road, Fah Hwa Village.

60 of the latter were permitted by the British Military to enter by the Rockhill Avenue barrier on September 1st, 1939 while the other 100 men, unarmed, crossed the Soochow Creek by boat at a point behind the Kung Dah Cotton Mill, 138 Jessfield Road, O.C.L., on the night of September 2/3, 1939, and were transported to the School billets by motor trucks. The passage of two trucks loaded with these policemen from west to east onto Jessfield Road crossing Brenan Road was noticed by several residents there on that night.

The 100 police constables of the Special Police Reserve Unit stationed in the Western District Police Bureau, 92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., arrived from Pootung at the beginning of August and entered the enclaves by the same method.

It will be noted that there was a bridge called
San Kwan Dong Bridge spanning the Soochow Creek
connecting an unnamed road to the north of Jessfield
Road (behind the Kung Dah Cotton Mill) on the south
side, with the Kwang Foh Road on the north side but
same was burned down by Chinese troops immediately
after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in August, 1937. The bridge has not been rebuilt
but a private ferry service by native boats went
into operation some time after the withdrawal of the
Chinese from Shanghai in November, 1937. It is
reported that this ferry service is also being made
use of for transporting opium from north of the creek
for sale by opium hongs in the Jessfield Area.

to adopt strong attitude towards Settlement Police.
Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (DIVISIONS) 25 AUG. 1939）
D. C. Divs
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 24 AUG. 1939）
F!
Cat.

From a usually reliable source, it has been
learned that following the Jessfield Road incident
which occurred on August 19, 1939, the constables
and officers attached to the Western District Police
Bureau, 92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., have been exhorted
to adopt a strong and undaunted attitude towards the
Settlement Police. They were informed that they
are at liberty to use force against any one, irrespect-
ive of nationality, who should dare to interfere with
their functions in the outside roads area in the
Western District. To each constable wounded during
the execution of his duty, they were assured, compen-
sation of $500.00 will be issued and for each one kill-
ed under such circumstances, a sum of $2,000.00 will
be granted to his family. The amount of compensation
will be increased to as much as $20,000.00 in accordance
with the rank and years of service with the organ.
It has been ascertained that the families of
Chang Zao Chong (張兆昌), a sub-inspector, and Chang
Kung Toh (張貢鐸), a sergeant of the Western District
Police Bureau, who were killed on August 19 in
Jessfield Road, have been promised a monthly subsidy
of $80.00 and $40.00 respectively in addition to a
lump sum of $300.00 each for funeral expenses.

A.C. (Special Branch) Sir:
Information
Liao Chung Chen
D. S. I.
R. H. Yorke

Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government -
Organization, personnel and present strength

In accordance with the Regulations Governing the
Organization of Police Force enacted by the Ministry of
Interior of the "Reformed Government," all the branch
bureaux, hitherto known as "Feng Joh" (分 局) and
stations or "Soo" (所) of the Shanghai City Government
Police have been renamed Police Bureaux or "Zu" (署)
since July, 1939. For instance, the "Western District
Branch Police Bureau" is now known as the "Western District
Police Bureau" and the "Lincoln Avenue Police Station" is
known as the "Lincoln Avenue Police Bureau."

On July 1, 1939, the police bureaux at Kating and
Tsungming Island, hitherto attached to the Kiangsu
Provincial Government of the "Reformed Government," were
brought under the control of the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau for the purpose of facilitating supervision
by the Japanese Special Service Section. Kying Yu Su
(金 玉 壽) alias Kying Dien Yang (金 殿 揚), and
Ying Tsung-lih (殷 仲 礼), Chief of the Feng Shien Police
Bureau, are in charge of the Kating Police Bureau and the
Tsungming Police Bureau respectively.

Hu Teh San (胡 德 山), Chief of the Lincoln
Avenue Police Bureau has been appointed Chief of the Feng
Shien Police Bureau. He has been replaced by Zung Song
(鄭 商).

Bao Tse-ying (鮑 子 英), deputy of the Detective
Corps has been appointed Chief of the River Police Main
Corps in succession to Hauh Liang Zung (霍 良 臣) who
has been appointed Chief of the "Greater Shanghai Youth
Corps."

上海市政府警察局 -
组织、人员及现有编制

根据“维新政府”内政部颁布的《警察队组织条例》，上海市政府警察局的所有分局，此前称为“分局” (Feng Joh) 和分所或“所” (Soo)，自1939年7月起已更名为警察局或“署” (Zu)。例如，“西区警察分局”现称为“西区警察署”，“林肯路警察所”现称为“林肯路警察署”。

1939年7月1日，原隶属于“维新政府”江苏省政府的嘉定和崇明岛警察局，为便于日本特务机关的监督，改归上海市政府警察局管辖。金玉壽 (Kying Yu Su)，又名金殿揚 (Kying Dien Yang)，以及奉贤警察局局长殷仲礼 (Ying Tsung-lih)，分别负责嘉定警察局和崇明警察局。

林肯路警察局局长胡德山 (Hu Teh San) 已被任命为奉贤警察局局长。其职位由郑商 (Zung Song) 接替。

侦探队副队长鲍子英 (Bao Tse-ying) 已被任命为水上警察总队队长，接替已被任命为“大上海青年团”团长的霍良臣 (Hauh Liang Zung)。

City Government Police Bureau.
Made by .................... and .................... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

This L.P. Sung or Sung Liang Fu (孫良夫),
in Chinese, is not the Lt. Col. Sung Li Ping (孫慶平),
former Secretary to General Yang Hu. The latter is a
native of Yangchow, Kiangpeh, whilst the former hailed
from Ningpo.

Inspector Sung Liang Fu or L.P. Sung claims
to have served in the Air Force of the Chinese Army.
His plane was brought down by Japanese in Hangchow in
1937 and he has since become an official of the new regime.
He is said to be the son-in-law of one Doong, the compra-
dore of Liddell Bros. Ltd., 4 Peking Road, a relative of
Fu Siao En.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Pootoo Road Station,
REPORT
Date 4th August, 1939.
Subject Passage along a Settlement Road by Armed Shanghai City Goverment
Police.
Made by S.I. Barton Forwarded by Jmmalson Inspector i/c.

Sir,
I beg to report that between 7 - 9 p.m. 3-8-39, I detailed 5 search parties and patrols to operate in this district rounding up loafers and other undesirables. The area covered was a triangle from the Hsia Sho Ferry along Ferry, Penang, Kiaochow and Robison Roads, including teashops.
One of the parties under Sub-Inspector Chiang was instructed to cover the Mei Fong Li, Robison Road, one of the principal hide out of loafers.
Special instructions were issued to be on the look-out for armed men in m/cars Vide Teleprinter Message in code of 6.41 p.m. 3-8-39.
At 7.25 p.m. Inspector Hsueh telephoned to the Station through street telephone box No. 4 (Robison & Hart Roads) reporting that this search party (S.I. Chiang in charge) had stopped a private motor car licence No. 8647 carrying armed S.C.G. Police from proceeding on to the Robison Road from the Mei Fong Lee.
On arrival at the alleyway the undersigned observed a black painted motor car (bearing no licence plate in front) parked at the mouth of the above alleyway with several S.C.G. policemen in uniform stretched across the alleyway with drawn Mauser pistols.
Together with Inspector Hsueh one Inspector L.P. Sung, attached to the Western Branch of the Shanghai City Goverment Police at No. 32 Jessfield Road, informed

日期 1939年8月4日。
主題 武裝上海市政府警察在租界道路通行。
呈報人 副督察長巴頓 (Barton) 由賈梅森 (Jmmalson) 督察長轉呈

先生，
謹此報告，1939年8月3日晚7至9時，我派遣了5個搜查組和巡邏隊在本區行動，圍捕閒散人員及其他不良分子。覆蓋區域為從下朔渡輪碼頭沿渡輪路、檳榔路、膠州路和羅便臣路形成的三角形地帶，包括茶館在內。
其中由蔣副督察長率領的一個小組受命負責羅便臣路美豐里一帶，該處是閒散人員的主要藏身地之一。
已發出特別指令，要求警惕汽車內的武裝人員。參見1939年8月3日下午6點41分的密碼電傳訊息。
晚上7點25分，薛督察通過街邊電話亭4號（羅便臣路與哈同路路口）致電本站，報告稱該搜查組（由蔣副督察長負責）攔截了一輛牌照號碼為 8647 的私家車，阻止載有武裝上海市政府警察的車輛從美豐里駛入羅便臣路。
抵達弄堂口時，本人看到一輛黑色塗裝的汽車（前部未掛牌照）停在上述弄堂口，幾名身穿制服的上海市政府警察橫跨弄堂，手持出鞘的毛瑟手槍。
與薛督察一同前來的還有隸屬上海市政府警察局西區分局（極司菲爾路32號）的 L.P. Sung 督察，他告知

the undersigned that at about 6.30 p.m. 3-1-39, he had
had occasion to proceed to the Mei Fong Li and was
proceeding back to his Station when he was stopped by the
search party. He admitted he had not applied for
permission for his armed party to proceed along the road-
way and apologised.

Mr. Yorke, D.O. "B", was communicated with by
telephone and informed of the incident who gave instructions
to escort the S.C.G. Police back to their station and to
inform them that in future should they wish to proceed

On returning to the Mei Fong Lee, a squad of about
20 Italian Marines under an officer Conte Giovanni
Bentivoglio who were on duty in the vicinity arrived on
the scene and was informed of what had taken place. He
conversed with Inspector Sung after which he disarmed all
the S.C.G. Police concerned and informed the undersigned
that he would escort them all back to their Station on
Jessfield Road.

The search party was withdrawn and ordered to patrol
another section.

The incident was settled at 8.15p.m. and normal
conditions resumed.

D.O. "B"

已通過電話聯繫「B」區巡官約克先生 (Mr. Yorke)，向其通報此事，他指示護送上海市政府警察返回其警局，並告知他們今後若希望在租界道路通行，應事先通知租界當局。

返回美豐里時，一支由孔特·喬瓦尼·本蒂沃利奧 (Conte Giovanni Bentivoglio) 軍官率領的約20名意大利海軍陸戰隊士兵正在附近執勤，他們趕到現場並獲悉了發生的一切。他與孫督察交談後，繳了所有涉事上海市政府警察的械，並告知本人他將護送他們全部返回極司菲爾路的警局。

搜查組撤離，並受命巡邏另一區域。

事件於晚上8點15分解決，秩序恢復正常。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No...........
Pootoo Road Station,
REPORT
Date 4th August, 1939.
Subject. Passage along a Settlement Road by Armed Shanghai City Government
Police.
Made by S.I. Chiang Ling Hsiang Forwarded by Jomaison Inspector i/c.

Sir,
I beg to report that acting on instructions, I was detailed on a stationary search party on Robison Road outside the Mei Fong Lee alleyway between 7 - 9 p.m. 3-8-39 with Hav. 195, S.P.C. 306, C.D.C. 50, C.P.Cs. 1886, 1896, 1904 and 1963. I was particularly instructed to be on on the alert for m/cars containing armed men.
At about 7.15 p.m. even date, we saw a black sedan motor car, Licence No. 8647, driving out from the Mei Fong Lee alleyway, carrying six civilians with four uniformed Shanghai City Government Policemen, holding Mauser pistols in their hands with two of them standing on each side of the running board pointing their weapons in the air. As the vehicle approached the search party, it was stopped when six male Chinese alighted from same and one of them in civilian clothes handed me a name card (attached), stating that he was Police Inspector Sung of the Municipal Government of Shanghai. At that time, a number of about 20 Ta Tao policemen with Mauser pistols in their hands rushed out from the Mei Fong Lee alleyway and surrounded the police search party, one of them pushing C.P.C. 1886 telling him to get out of the way. I immediately told C.D.C. 50 to inform our next search party under Inspector Hsueh at the corner of Robison and Kiaochow Roads and requested his assistance. I then informed Mr. Sung that he should first get permission before proceeding with an armed party along a Settlement Road and he apologized for the wrong procedure

Subject. Passage along a Settlement Road by Armed Shanghai City Government

Made by S.I. Chiang Ling Hsiang Forwarded by Jrmalson Inspector i/c.

Sir,
I beg to report that acting on instructions, I was
detailed on a stationary search party on Robison Road
outside the Mei Fong Lee alleyway between 7 - 9 p.m.
3-8-39 with Hav. 195, S.P.C. 306, C.D.C. 50, C.P.Cs. 1886,
1896, 1904 and 1963. I was particularly instructed to be
on the alert for m/cars containing armed men.
At about 7.15 p.m. even date, we saw a black sedan
motor car, Licence No. 8647, driving out from the Mei Fong
Lee alleyway, carrying six civilians with four uniformed
Shanghai City Government policemen, holding Mauser pistols in
their hands with two of them standing on each side of the
running board pointing their weapons in the air. As the
vehicle approached the search party, it was stopped when
six male Chinese alighted from same and one of them in
civilian clothes handed me a name card (attached), stating
that he was Police Inspector Sung of the Municipal Government
of Shanghai. At that time, a number of about 20 Ta Tao
policemen with Mauser pistols in their hands rushed out
from the Mei Fong Lee alleyway and surrounded the police
search party, one of them pushing C.P.C. 1886 telling him
to get out of the way. I immediately told C.D.C. 50 to
inform our next search party under Inspector Hsuch at the
corner of Robison and Kiaochow Roads and requested his
assistance. I then informed Mr. Sung that he should first
get permission before proceeding with an armed party along
a Settlement Road and he apologized for the wrong procedure

Date July 21 19 39.

Subject The Shanghai City Government Police Bureau being strengthened.

Made by. and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The Detective Department of the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau has not been re-organized,
but there has been a marked increase in the strength of
the Chinese Police Force and an expansion of their
control in accordance with an order received in June
from Chen Chun(陳羣), Minister of Interior of the
Reformed Government.

In accordance with the above instructions,
Lu Ying took over jurisdiction of two districts, viz:
Kating and Tsungming, on July 1st, which necessitated
an increase of 480 policemen over these districts.
In consequence, Ching Dien Yang(金殿揚), former
Secretary to Lu Ying, has been appointed Chief of Police
at Kating with a strength of 230 men, and Ying Chung Yu
(殷仲裕) has been appointed Chief of Police at
Tsungming with a strength of 220 men. Ying was formerly
Chief of the Fengyi Police. Hu Teh San(胡德山),
Inspector in charge of the Lincoln Road Sub-Station
(林肯路) has been transferred to Fengyi as Chief of
Police. Tseng Song(鄭商), Deputy Chief of the
Department of Justice (Headquarters), has been appointed
to take charge of Lincoln Road Sub-Station.

Pao Tsz Ying(鮑子英), Deputy Chief Detective
Officer who has established an office at 92 Jessfield
Road, has been appointed to take charge of the Water
Police.

（左侧椭圆印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 23 JULY 1939 INTELLIGENCE OFFICE）

Commr of Police

制作人及转发人 谭绍良（Tan Shao Liang）警司

上海市政府警察局侦缉处尚未重组，但根据维新政府内政部长陈群（Chen Chun）于六月下达的命令，华警部队的人数显著增加，其管辖范围也有所扩大。

根据上述指示，陆英（Lu Ying）于七月一日接管了两个区的管辖权，即：嘉定和崇明，这导致这两个区的警力增加了480名警察。因此，陆英的前秘书金殿扬（Ching Dien Yang）被任命为嘉定警察局局长，辖下警力230人；殷仲裕（Ying Chung Yu）被任命为崇明警察局局长，辖下警力220人。殷曾任奉义警察局局长。负责林肯路（Lincoln Road）分所的胡德山（Hu Teh San）巡官已调往奉义担任警察局局长。司法部（总部）副主任郑商（Tseng Song）已被任命负责林肯路分所。

鲍子英（Pao Tsz Ying），副主任侦探长，已在杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road，今万航渡路）92号设立办公室，已被任命负责水上警察。

TAIRIKU SHIMPO 15·7 3

THE SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT POLICE BUREAU
BEING STRENGTHENED : DETECTIVE CORPS REORGANIZED

The Shanghai City Government Police
Bureau has increased its personnel and is going to reform
its organization, aiming at simplification of police work
and promotion of efficiency.
As the first step, the
reorganization of the Detective Corps has been decided: The
Special Branch will henceforth become independant of other
branches of the Detective Corps in order to cope with the
development of social affairs in the area under the control
of the City Government.
Following this reorganization,
other departments will be reformed in the near future.
pages.zh:
《大陆新报》 15·7 3

上海市政府警察局力量加强：侦缉队重组

上海市政府警察局已增加人员，并计划改革其组织结构，旨在简化警务工作并提高效率。
作为第一步，已决定重组侦缉队：特别支部今后将独立于侦缉队的其他部门，以应对市政府控制区域内社会事务的发展。
继此次重组之后，其他部门将在不久的将来进行改革。

Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government -
Organization, personnel and present strength

The Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government
at present comprises eleven branch bureaux, five police
stations and eight other police units including the
detective corps, the garrison corps, the police reserve
unit, the river police corps, the police training depot,
the police band, the detention house and the police
hospital, with a total strength of 5,662. Compared with
the complement functioning at the end of April, 1939, the
present strength represents an increase of 507. This
classification according to rank is as follows :-

In accordance with the instructions of Mayor
Fu Siao-en of the Shanghai City Government, Loo Ying,
Commissioner of the police bureau, ordered at the
beginning of May, 1939, the establishment of a new branch
bureau at Nanchiao, in Feng Shien District, Pootung,
because of the improved conditions in that area. This
branch is under the charge of one Ying Tsung Lih (殷仲禮), but is
functioning under the direction of M. Yamashita, Chief of
the Feng Shien Section of the Japanese Military Special
Service Section. Some 220 constables are attached to
this branch and are armed with about 100 rifles of a
miscellaneous type.

Prior to March, 1939, Chinese guerilla units were
active in and around Nanchiao, which was at times under
their complete control. From the beginning of March,
however, the Sungkiang Garrison of the Japanese forces
under one Nakajima, launched a drive against these
guerillas and following intensive mopping up operations,
which lasted about one month, compelled the latter to
withdraw. Since that time the population has continued
to increase and at the end of April, 1939, the inhabitants
numbered some 4,000. Some 120 troops (Japanese) belong-
ing to the Sungkiang garrison are still stationed there.

A police band numbering 33, under Moo Kuo Liang
(馬國良), was formed during May, by Loo Ying, Commissioner
of Police, with the approval of Mayor Fu Siao-en.

On May 12, 1939, twenty cadets who had completed
their training in the police academy of the Ministry of
Interior of the Reformed Government, Nanking, arrived in
Shanghai. Since their arrival they have been attached
pages.zh:
- 2 -

根据上海市政府市长傅筱庵的指示，警察局局长陆英（Loo Ying）于1939年5月初下令在浦东奉贤区南桥设立一个新的分局，因为该地区的局势有所改善。该分局由殷仲礼（Ying Tsung Lih）负责，但在日本军方特务机关奉贤section负责人山下（M. Yamashita）的指导下运作。该分局配有约220名警员，武装有约100支杂式步枪。

1939年3月之前，中国游击队在南桥及其周边地区活动频繁，该地区有时完全处于他们的控制之下。然而，从3月初开始，驻松江的中岛（Nakajima）率领的日军对这批游击队发动了攻势，经过持续约一个月的密集清剿行动，迫使后者撤退。自那时起，人口持续增加，到1939年4月底，居民人数约为4,000人。仍有约120名日军士兵驻扎在那里，隶属于松江卫戍部队。

一支由33人组成的警察乐队，由马国良（Moo Kuo Liang）领导，于5月经警察局局长陆英组建，并获市长傅筱庵批准。

1939年5月12日，二十名在南京维新政府内政部警察学院完成训练的学员抵达上海。自抵达以来，他们已被分配

pages.en:
- 3 -

to the various branch bureaux with the rank of sub-
inspector. The police bureau has at present some 210
sub-inspectors on its strength.

In consequence of the increase in personnel and
the volume of work the bureau has had to cope with,
the monthly appropriation of $160,000 has been found
insufficient to cover expenses and beginning from May,
the allotment has been increased to $200,000 upon the
recommendation of Mayor Fu Siao-en.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No...........
Section 1, Special Br.
REPORT
Date May, 15 19 39.

Subject (in full) "Police Officers Training Institute" in Nanking - graduates sent
to Shanghai for service with the "Shanghai City Government Police Bureau".
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. O J

On May 12, 20 graduates from the "Police
Officers Training Institute" (警官學校) of the
"Ministry of the Interior of the Reformed Government"
in Nanking, arrived in Shanghai and were allocated to
the various branches of the "Police Bureau of the
Shanghai City Government" as "Extra-Sub-Inspectors"
at $60.- each per month. They constitute the
first batch of graduates from the "Police Officers
Training Institute", of which Chen Chun (陳群),
Minister of the Interior of the "Reformed Government",
is the principal.

Subject... Western District Police Branch Bureau - sub-stations and outposts
supplied with firearms.
Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Crawford O.J

At the request of Wong Tuh Ling (王德林), chief
of the Western District Branch Police Bureau, 92
Jessfield Road, U.O.L., the Japanese military autho-
rities recently supplied two rifles and one .auser
pistol to each of the following eight sub-stations and
outposts in the extra-Settlement road area in the
Western District (within the perimeter):-

1. Zau Ka Doo Sub-station, 1362 Jessfield Road.
2. Rouison Road Sub-station, 38 Rouison Road.
3. Edinburgh Road Outpost, Lane 469, 40 Edinburgh Road.
4. Brenan Road Outpost, 553 Brenan Road.
5. Rouison Road Outpost, 733 Rouison Road.
6. Wah Sui Loong Outpost, Lane 1051, 51 Ferry Road.
7. Kong Ka Chiao Outpost, 124 Kong Ka Chiao, Connaught
Road.
8. Singapore Road Outpost, 478 Singapore Road.

To one rifle or pistol, five rounds of ammunition
are issued while officers in charge of the sub-stations
and outposts have been warned that they are solely
responsible for the loss of the firearms or their
misuse.

It will be recalled that the Japanese military
only supplied the Western District Branch Police
Bureau with 40 rifles and 20 pistols and one round
of ammunition to each rifle or pistol (Vide Special
Branch report dated 7/2/39).

March 7, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Ying Yeh Pao dated Mar.6:

A CHINESE GENDARMERIE CORPS

Loo Ying (盧英), Commissioner of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, has become scared for no fewer than 1,000 Japanese and puppet soldiers have been killed during recent attacks by guerrillas in the suburbs of Shanghai. With the permission of the Japanese authorities, he has selected 400 short and sturdy puppet policemen and trained them into a gendarmerie corps; each man is armed with a rifle and 50 rounds of ammunition. 200 members of this corps will be stationed in the Criminal Investigation Department room at the Headquarters of the Police Bureau, while the remaining 200 will be distributed equally among the branch Bureaux in the Western District and Pootung.

Yesterday morning, Loo Ying assembled the gendarmerie corps and instructed them not to speak so as to avoid being discovered by the people. Each member is given a monthly pay of $30, while a senior officer is given $50.

Judging by the above, the military strength of the Japanese seems to be very weak. With the exception of a section of the Japanese Naval Landing Party in Shanghai, all Japanese soldiers have been transferred to Hainan Island.

3月6日《大英夜报》：

一支中国宪兵队

上海市政府警察局局长卢英（盧英），因近期游击队在上海郊区袭击中杀害了不下1000名日本人和伪军士兵而感到恐慌。经日本当局许可，他挑选了400名身材矮小但结实的伪警察，将其训练成一支宪兵队；每人配备一支步枪和50发子弹。该队200名成员将驻扎在警察局总部的侦缉队房间，其余200名则平均分配至西区和浦东的分局。

昨天上午，卢英集结了这支宪兵队，并指示他们不要说话，以免被民众发现。每名成员月薪30元，高级官员月薪50元。

据此判断，日军的军事力量似乎非常薄弱。除上海日本海军陆战队的一部分外，所有日本士兵已调往海南岛。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. REGISTRY

Branch Shibun
Date February 24. 39.

Subject Western District Branch Police Bureau - patrolling groups
reorganized - further ammunition issued.

Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung-chien Forwarded by.

The patrolling groups of the Western District
Branch Police Bureau have been recently reorganized.
There are at present six patrolling groups of five
constables each as compared with eight groups of ten
constables each before the reorganization (Vide
Special Branch report dated 7/2/39). The fifty
constables from those groups have now been put on
traffic, point and general patrol duty.

Four of the five constables in one patrolling
group are armed with rifles while the remaining one
is armed with a pistol. To one rifle or pistol four
additional rounds of ammunition have been issued by
the Japanese Authorities at the request of Wong Tuh
Ling (王德林), Chief of the Branch Bureau, in view
of the successive outrages committed by armed gangsters
in the Western District, O.O.L. It will be recalled
that prior to February 7, 1939, only one round of
ammunition was issued to one rifle or pistol as a
precaution against possible mutiny on the part of the
police constables.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.

西区分局警察局的巡逻组最近进行了重组。目前共有六个巡逻组，每组五名巡捕，而重组前为八个组，每组十名巡捕（参见39年2月7日的特别处报告）。来自这些组的五十名巡捕现在已被安排执行交通、定点和一般巡逻任务。

一个巡逻组中的五名巡捕，有四名配备步枪，另一名配备手枪。鉴于越界筑路区西区武装匪徒连续作案，应分局局长王德林（王德林）的请求，日本当局为每支步枪或手枪增发了四发额外弹药。需指出的是，在1939年2月7日之前，为防止巡捕可能发生的哗变，每支步枪或手枪仅配发一发弹药。

Subject Western District Branch Police Bureau - to adopt strong attitude
        towards the Settlement Authorities.
Made by                     Forwarded by

It has been confidentially learned that the
Western District Branch Police Bureau, 92 Jessfield
Road, O.O.L., has been instructed by the "Shanghai
City Government" to stiffen its attitude towards the
Settlement Authorities regarding matters concerning
jurisdiction over the extra-Settlement area in the
Western District.

On February 7, 1939, four light machine guns and
four heavy machine guns were conveyed to the Bureau
by the Japanese Military Police but no ammunition was
supplied. According to instructions the ammunition
will be supplied when required, from the Western Section
of the Japanese Military Police (now known as Kaneya
Military Police Detachment), 94 Jessfield Road, situated
next to the Bureau.

The Japanese Military, in arming the police with
machine guns, would appear to aim at giving confidence
to the policemen that they will have the support of the
former in case any trouble occurs.

Certified true copy.
H. C. Sandley

on the part of the police constables.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.2, Special Branch Tibet,
REPORT
Date February 1, 1939.

Subject Organization, Personnel and Strength of the Police Bureau
of the "Shanghai City Government".

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang

There are under the Police Bureau of the "Shanghai
City Government", ten Branch Bureaux, four Police Stations
and five other police units equivalent in status to a
Branch Bureau, including the Detective Corps, the Garrison
Corps, the Youths' Corps, the Police Reserve Unit and the
River Police Main Corps.

The number of ranking officers and other senior
personnel of the Bureau are given below :-

Commissioner 1
D.C. (Secretary) 1
A.C. (Special Deputy) 2
Superintendents (Chiefs of the various 5
Departments, Headquarters)
Chief Inspectors (Chiefs of the various 15
Corps and Officers i/c Branch
Bureaux)
Inspectors (Officer i/c Stations) 40
Sub-Inspectors (Officers i/c Sub- 80
Stations and other officers on
patrol)
Sergeants 340
Constables 2,960
3,444

A large number of Sub-Stations and Outposts which
are in the charge of officers holding the rank of Sub-
Inspectors and Sergeants respectively, are established in
the various localities under the jurisdiction of the Bureau.

Attached hereto is a list of Departments, Branch
Bureaux, Stations and Sub-Stations of the Police Bureau

pages.en:
Section 1, Special Branch,
January 24, 1939.

Western Branch Police Bureau - notice re jurisdiction
over Western District.
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

On January 22, 1939, copies of a notice were posted
outside the various sections and sub-sections of the Police
Bureau in the Western District, O.O.I. regarding the
jurisdiction over the extra-Settlement road area. A full
translation of the notice reads as follows:-

WESTERN BRANCH OF THE SHANGHAI POLICE BUREAU -
NOTICE
----------------

It is a custom that the residents in the extra-
Settlement road area in the Western District report all
cases relating to peace and order to the Settlement Police.
Such procedure is wrong for the S.M.P. have jurisdiction
over the roads only and not the areas between these roads
which are Chinese controlled territories.

The people in the Western District are hereby warned
that hereafter they should report all cases to the Western
Branch Police Bureau instead of to the S.M.P.

Wong Teh Ling (王志林)
Chief of the Western
Branch Police Bureau.
January, 1939.

Certified true copy

H. C. Eardley
THI/o

西区警察局 - 关于对西区管辖权的通告。
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

1939年1月22日，在越界筑路（O.O.I.）西区警察局的各科及分科外张贴了关于对越界筑路区域管辖权的通告副本。该通告的完整译文如下：-

上海警察局西区分局 -
通告
----------------

西区越界筑路区域的居民习惯将所有涉及治安的案件向租界警察报案。此种做法是错误的，因为上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）仅对道路拥有管辖权，而这些道路之间的区域属于中国控制领土。

特此警告西区民众，此后所有案件应向西区警察局报案，而非向上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）报案。

Wong Teh Ling (王志林)
西区警察局局长。
1939年1月。

核证无误副本

H. C. Eardley
THI/o
